prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create a polished, high-fidelity native Windows game-launcher concept for The Order: 1886. This is composition C, a configuration-focused command sheet. Render one complete desktop app window, straight-on, landscape 3:2, crisp and readable, without a surrounding desktop or external presentation labels.

Input image is a reference for the existing game's artwork, charcoal/brass/ivory palette and serif wordmark only. Keep that visual world, but build a materially different, practical form-led composition. Show the armored protagonist and misty Victorian London street as a shallow, beautifully cropped panoramic artwork banner across the top quarter of the app, with "THE ORDER" / "1886" in brass serif at the left. Keep a slim native dark Windows title bar above the banner.

The lower three-quarters is one calm, broad charcoal operating sheet, not a stack of cards. Give the controls room to breathe within a centered content measure. A full-width "Game folder" row shows a native field "…\CUSA00076", "Change" button and restrained "Game files found" status. Below a quiet rule, show a single balanced row of three large native dropdowns: "Display" / "Borderless", "Upscaling" / "FSR 1", and "Frame rate" / "30 FPS". Below them, two tidy native checkboxes read "VSync" and "Performance overlay (F9)". Both are checked.

Anchor the bottom of this sheet with a clear action row: a quiet "Settings" action and secondary "Verify files" / "View logs" on the left, a large matte brass "Play" button on the right. Keep the exact warning "Experimental runtime. Gameplay is not yet verified." visible directly above the action row. Prioritize confident legibility and a clear path to launch, with less art dominance than the other layouts.

Visual grammar: charcoal #0b0b0a, brass #d4bd75, ivory #e9e5d8, warm muted text #a8a497. Serif only for the wordmark; readable Windows humanist sans for all UI. Native rectangular controls with subtly softened corners, careful alignment, strong text hierarchy and deliberate spacing. Flat surfaces, understated separators and no unnecessary framing. One dominant primary action.

Use only the real launcher capabilities above. The selected 30 FPS is a configuration choice, not a measured FPS. No fake telemetry, benchmarks, certified-playable claim, account, store, downloads, mod manager or invented options. Avoid badges above headings, section numbers, card grids, ornamental borders, decorative gradients/glass/blur, extra emblems and unrelated branding. The result must look buildable as a real Windows desktop launcher.
